bullets.title: Post-election AI capex rotation: DC infrastructure falls, non-AI cyclicals surge
bullets.body: Buildout baskets fell from -1% to -11% post-midterms while Homebuilders +8% and Retailers +5.5%. Market is removing policy-driven supply shocks and AI-led inflationary risk from distribution, with Texas/Georgia data center moratorium risks emerging (TX represents ~27% of MW funded by high-yield). JPM now questions 62+ GW of 2028 capacity; DC PTO forecast cut from 122.4 GW to 112.8 GW for 2026-2030E.

bullets.title: Semis/DC complex -3%+ on regulatory risk; hyperscaler rotation into app-layer software
bullets.body: AI semis and memory names sold off 3-10%+ (AMD -5%, QCOM -10%, ARM -4.5%, GFS -5.8%) as midterm results raised datacenter moratorium fears. Simultaneously, hedge funds rotated hard into Software/SaaS (+1.6σ) and Hyperscalers (+1.1σ); internet stocks outperformed software 5.5x with KWEB +4.5% vs IGV +1%. Mega-cap tech (MSFT, GOOGL, AAPL, AMZN) added over $1T market cap as investors fled to perceived compute value.

bullets.title: S&P correlations at historic lows (0.6th percentile 6mo), stock-picking regime in full force
bullets.body: S&P stock correlations are at the 0.6th percentile on a 6-month basis and 4.7th percentile on 1-month, indicating an unusually strong stock-picking environment. Cash Return factor continues to work; momentum unwind is the second-largest decline since the GFC but positioning at 47th percentile on a 5-year lookback signals an attractive entry point per JPM.

bullets.title: Upcoming macro catalysts: CPI Nov 10, PPI Nov 13, Fed Dec 9
bullets.body: Key macro data points for the week ahead include CPI on November 10 and PPI on November 13. The Fed's next meeting is December 9. US-China trade truce has been extended through January 20, 2027. Market tolerance for an upside inflation print seen as higher given AI equity drawdown risk and lower oil prices.

bullets.title: Data center debt market tightening: $100B+ issuance in 2026, spreads widening
bullets.body: Data center debt issuance surpassed $100B in 2026 vs. $73B prior year, but spreads have widened and financing costs have increased. JPM/MS project $40-50B of incremental gross securitized DC credit issuance in 2027, but future growth is now contingent on debt market access. Shares in DC-linked names like CSQR are down 30%+ since IPO on rising rates, softening AI infrastructure sentiment, and unproven execution.

bullets.title: QCOM: datacenter momentum real ($5B FY27 target) but handset drag and margin miss send stock -10%
bullets.body: QCOM reported in-line revenue but Dec quarter EPS guidance of $2.25 came in below consensus of $2.33, driven by handset weakness (~28% YoY decline to $17B) and Apple insourcing. Datacenter AI revenue targeting $5B in FY27 (~10% of sales) with a ~$7B exit run rate. Citi cuts FY27/F28 EPS by 17%/12%.

bullets.title: ARM: AGI CPU opportunity raised to $2B in FY27-28 but mobile royalty miss drags stock -7%
bullets.body: ARM licensing beat +27% YoY on 3 new ATAs and 4 CSS deals; datacenter royalties doubled YoY for the third consecutive quarter, with hyperscaler server share tracking to >60% by end-CY26. However, mobile royalties missed and royalty revenue of $670M came in below GS/Street estimates, sending stock down ~7%. Management raised AGI CPU revenue guidance to up to $2B across FY27/FY28 (vs prior >$1B).

bullets.title: COHR: 45% gross margin target by CY28, $20B NPO LTA — most bullish AI-optics print of the cycle
bullets.body: COHR reported Sep-Q revenue of $2.37B and guided Dec-Q to $2.55-2.75B, well above Street. Management raised long-term gross margin target to above 45% (from above 42%) and secured a ~$20B five-year LTA with a major AI datacenter customer for NPO scale-up. Datacenter revenue grew 85% YoY; FY27 pro forma revenue growth expected above 60%. Citi raised PT to $440 on 30x FY2028E EPS of ~$16.5.

bullets.title: MRVL-LITE merger: combined silicon-optics solution for XPU scale-up; combined decline ~40% since announcement
bullets.body: Jefferies frames the MRVL-LITE merger rationale as an optimized silicon-optics solution for scale-up/scale-in XPU architectures. However, the combined entity has declined ~40% since the deal announcement, reflecting broader AI infrastructure sentiment deterioration and integration uncertainty.

bullets.title: APP: strongest topline beat in 6 quarters; $9-10B FY27 EBITDA guide 10%+ above Street
bullets.body: APP delivered 55% revenue growth with 84% EBITDA margins in Q3, driven by new Axon model architecture and gaming up nearly 50% YoY. FY27 Adj. EBITDA guidance of $9.0B-$10.0B was 10%+ above Street's $8.6B. Q4 guide implies +10% QoQ growth. FY27 GAAP EPS potential of $21-$23 implies a 10x P/E floor, and APP announced a $3.2B buyback.

bullets.title: Post-midterm hyperscaler thesis: regulation paradoxically raises their moat vs China
bullets.body: Multiple sources note that increased regulatory scrutiny of US hyperscalers (MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL, META) post-midterms paradoxically increases their asset value versus unregulated Chinese competitors. META's president flagged that midterm results will make US data center expansion harder and that the company is considering builds outside the US. Apple has separately cut internal AI spending budgets to reduce costs.

bullets.title: Asian AI names look like tactical buy post-pullback; JPM prefers defined-risk structures on NKY, HSTECH, KOSPI2
bullets.body: JPM argues the pullback in Asia AI names looks overdone versus still-supportive fundamentals, with US midterm uncertainty now cleared and macro risks stabilizing. Taiwan chip stocks are discounting a slowdown with earnings growth moderating from +70% YoY in 2026 to +41%/+31% in 2027-28. JPM prefers call spread structures for NKY, HSTECH, and KOSPI2 KO calls.

bullets.title: HUBS: FY26 guide cut to $945-947M vs Street $965M; Q4 bookings collapse to 12% growth
bullets.body: HubSpot guided Q4 revenue at 12% YoY growth vs Street's expectation, and net adds declined to 5,250 vs. 7,000 prior quarter, signaling deteriorating demand in the mid-market SaaS vertical. Shares fell 8%+ premarket.

bullets.title: SNAP ad revenue deceleration (4% vs 9% prior) signals broader digital ad risk beyond AI winners
bullets.body: SNAP Q3 ad revenue slowed to +4% YoY from +9% in Q2, with DAUs below Street; shares fell 10.5% premarket. NYT showing potential traffic headwinds from Google AI Overviews impacting ad revenue. AI expansion is broadly benefiting the digital ad market per JPM tech, but platform-level execution divergence is widening.

bullets.title: CSCO downgraded to EW at Morgan Stanley; pullforward risk and AI margin pressure after 43% 12-month rally
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley cut CSCO from Overweight to Equal-Weight and lowered PT from $135 to $120, arguing risk/reward is now balanced after the stock rerated to S&P 500 parity at ~19x forward earnings versus its historical 20% discount. AI cloud orders are lower-margin (~30-40% hardware margins vs enterprise portfolio), and pricing increases mirror FFIV/FTNT pullforward patterns.

bullets.title: Micron suspends $4.5B Taiwan plant; Intel CEO buys 150K shares — semis signals diverging
bullets.body: Micron suspended its $4.5B Taiwan memory-chip plant construction amid a labor dispute, adding to near-term supply-side uncertainty. Separately, Intel's CEO purchased 150K shares at a $64.73 weighted average price, a rare insider-buying signal for a stock that has been a persistent underperformer.

bullets.title: Open-source AI threatens frontier developer pricing power — Acemoglu (MIT) cautious on ROI
bullets.body: MIT economist Daron Acemoglu argues that cheaper open-weight models are undermining the pricing power of OpenAI, Anthropic, and other frontier developers, and that the US is overinvesting in foundation models while underdeveloping practical applications. He sees worker-enhancing AI tools in healthcare, education, and engineering as the more durable economic opportunity.

bullets.title: Market breadth strongest in 120 days (NYSE A/D +1426), but semis/AI names expected to continue lower
bullets.body: NYSE advancing stocks beat declining by 1,426 issues — the best reading in 120 days — with NYSE Cumulative Breadth turning positive above an improving 21-day MA. Financials participation (KBW back above 200-day MA) is confirming market health. However, technical analysis suggests AI, semis, and memory stocks will continue to act poorly and decline further.

bullets.title: Cable broadband narrative worsens: fiber at $30-40/mo + Verizon mmWave FWA expanding by 10-15M homes
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley cut CHTR PT to $135 from $140 as Cox KPI disclosures reveal steeper broadband losses than legacy Charter, amid aggressive fiber pricing ($30-40/month) and Verizon's new 1Gbps FWA mmWave solution expanding the addressable fixed wireless market by 10-15M homes. CHTR described as having the weakest medium-term growth algorithm in US Telco/Cable.

bullets.title: Gildan FY26 EPS guidance cut 17-19% signals weak mass-channel, low-income consumer demand
bullets.body: Gildan lowered FY26 EPS guidance to $3.70-$3.80 from $4.65-$4.75 and revenue guidance to $5.4-5.5B from $6.0-6.2B (~8% below consensus), with 4Q pro-forma revenue expected down ~16% YoY. Results signal a deteriorating demand environment for mass-channel and low-income consumer businesses; company withdrew its 2026-2028 guidance targets entirely.
